message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Nix

on:
  pull_request:
  push:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Setup
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y mariadb-client
    - name: Cache Cargo dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          ~/.cargo/git
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
    - name: Run tests
      run: cargo test --verbose
  nix:
    needs: [test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v25
      with:
        nix_path: nixpkgs=channel:nixos-unstable
    - name: Nix flake check
      run: nix flake check
    - name: Test nix build
      run: | 
        nix run . -- --help | grep -qE "Usage: geni( \[OPTIONS\])? <COMMAND>" || exit 2",
  "rationale": "The repository is a Rust project with a Cargo.lock, and the test job runs `cargo test --verbose`, which fetches crates from the registry on every run. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern, supported by measured experiments caching Go modules and Gradle dependencies, recommends caching dependency download state keyed on the lockfile while keeping all required tests. Adding an actions/cache step for ~/.cargo/registry and ~/.cargo/git keyed on Cargo.lock preserves every existing step and coverage, adds no new network access, secrets, privileges, or publishing/deployment operations, and there is no equivalent cache already present in the workflow.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200"]
}
